title: Binary Tree Maximum Path Sum
oneLinerQuestion: Find the maximum sum of any non-empty path between two nodes in a binary tree.
explanation:
Problem Intuition: The Binary Tree Maximum Path Sum problem asks for the maximum sum of any non-empty path along connected nodes in a binary tree, where each node can appear at most once. A path may peak at an arbitrary node acting as an arch (joining paths from both its left and right subtrees), but when returning a value upward to its parent, only a single branch (either left or right) can be extended. By performing a post-order Depth-First Search (DFS), we can calculate the best gain each node contributes upward while simultaneously evaluating whether turning through that node produces a new global maximum path.

- Step 1: Global Maximum Initialization — We initialize a global variable `maxSum = -Infinity` to track the highest path sum discovered across the entire tree, ensuring proper handling of trees containing only negative node values.

- Step 2: Recursive Helper Definition — We define a helper function `maxGain(node)` that computes the maximum path sum that starts at `node` and extends downward into at most one of its subtrees.

- Step 3: Base Case (Null Nodes) — If `node === null`, an empty branch contributes no value, so we return `0`.

- Step 4: Subtree Gain Calculation & Negative Pruning — We recursively compute the maximum gains from the left and right subtrees: `const leftGain = Math.max(maxGain(node.left), 0)` and `const rightGain = Math.max(maxGain(node.right), 0)`. Negative gains are clamped to 0 using `Math.max(..., 0)` because omitting a negative-sum subtree is always preferable to including it.

- Step 5: Arch Path Evaluation & Global Update — The maximum path sum that peaks at the current node (using the node as the turning point connecting both branches) is `currentArchSum = node.val + leftGain + rightGain`. We update the overall record: `maxSum = Math.max(maxSum, currentArchSum)`.

- Step 6: Upward Branch Return — To allow an ancestor to use this node as part of its path, we can only continue along one branch. We return the node's value plus the larger of its two subtrees: `return node.val + Math.max(leftGain, rightGain)`.

- Step 7: Termination & Result Return — We initiate the traversal by calling `maxGain(root)`. Once the recursive traversal completes across all nodes, `maxSum` holds the maximum path sum.

- Complexity & Memory Guarantees — Time Complexity: O(N) where N is the total number of nodes, as each node is visited exactly once. Space Complexity: O(H) auxiliary space on the call stack, where H is the height of the tree (O(log N) for balanced trees, O(N) for skewed trees).
pseudoCode:
FUNCTION maxPathSum(root):
    maxSum = -INFINITY
    FUNCTION getMaxGain(node):
        IF node IS NULL THEN RETURN 0
        leftGain = MAX(getMaxGain(node.left), 0)
        rightGain = MAX(getMaxGain(node.right), 0)
        maxSum = MAX(maxSum, node.val + leftGain + rightGain)
        RETURN node.val + MAX(leftGain, rightGain)
    END FUNCTION
    getMaxGain(root)
    RETURN maxSum
END FUNCTION
